hypotheses.title: Union of N record types is O(N^2) time and memory in top-level type resolution (left-fold BDD union rebuilds the whole middle chain, plus eager key interning of every intermediate BDD node)
hypotheses.issue: `A|B|C|...` parses as a left-nested binary union, so resolveBTypeInner (BLangUnionTypeNode) computes Union(Union(Union(A,B),C),D)... via semtypes.Union -> mappingOps.Union -> bddSubtypeUnion -> bddUnion/bddUnionWithMemo/bddUnionInner. BDD atoms are ordered by creation index (atomCmp); each new record's atom is larger than every atom in the accumulator, so bddUnionInner always takes the cmp>0... path down the `middle` chain and rebuilds it: step i creates ~i new BDD nodes, ~N^2/2 overall. Two constant-factor costs dominate on top of that: (1) every newly created bddNodeImpl eagerly interns its canonical key through internBddNodeKey (global mutex + global map that is never freed), ~47% of CPU and the bulk of the resident memory, although most intermediate nodes never have their key requested; (2) every bddUnion call allocates a fresh bddOpMemo (three maps) and inserts i entries, although a union with a single-atom node walks one path and never gets a memo hit (~340 MB allocated at N=2000). Writing the union in reverse order (R{N-1}|...|R0) is linear (N=4000: 45 ms vs 19 s), confirming it is the union strategy. The asymptotic O(N^2) node count is inherent while every intermediate BLangUnionTypeNode must carry its prefix-union type (type resolution validators require it) and BDDs are atom-ordered; going fully linear would need an n-ary union AST node or relaxing that rule.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a valid Ballerina program defining N closed record types and one
union type `Event` of all N (written R0|R1|...|R{N-1}), then using it trivially.
Usage: python3 gen_union.py N > union_N.bal"""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = ["import ballerina/io;", ""]
for i in range(n):
    out.append(f"type R{i} record {{| int id{i}; string name; |}};")
out.append("")
out.append("type Event " + "|".join(f"R{i}" for i in range(n)) + ";")
out.append("")
out.append("public function main() {")
out.append('    Event e = {id0: 1, name: "x"};')
out.append("    io:println(e is R0);")
out.append("}")
print("\n".join(out))

hypotheses.fix_approach: Two changes in semtypes, no behaviour change (BDDs identical node-for-node, goldens untouched): (1) bddNodeImpl interns its canonical key lazily on first canonicalKey() call (stored in an atomic.Int64, 0 = unset; children are interned before the parent so the bottom-up uniqueness argument still holds; racing goroutines get the same key because the interner returns the existing entry; atom keys are immutable). (2) bddUnion short-circuits when either operand is a *bddNodeSimple (single atom: left=All, middle=right=Nothing) into a memo-free bddUnionAtomNode that yields exactly what bddUnionInner would (smaller atom: recurse down middle; larger: bddCreate(atom, All, b, Nothing); equal: bddCreate(atom, All, middle, right)). Pitfall: flattening/reordering the union in the type resolver is not viable as-is because every intermediate BLangUnionTypeNode must have its (prefix) type set, and reordering would change type-string member order in goldens. Remaining O(N^2) is the node allocations themselves. make test and make test-race pass.
